answer: A stake-and-reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit that is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving, and each verified job adds a pearl of trust to its record. A brand-new identity starts as a barren oasis — visible but with no history to draw on — so it can only take tiny, low-value jobs until it earns standing, like yarrow spreading slowly from a single root. Spinning up thousands of fakes then costs thousands of deposits and months of honest work, which prices the attack out of reach.
